transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm having some trouble at work. I just can't seem to keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. Even when it's really important. 

I do computer support, and... I'll start tracing a client's network problem, and maybe ten minutes later I'll realize I've just reread the same log entries three times. And I still don't know what they say. So... yeah. That's what brings me in.
Have you struggled with this kind of difficulty focusing since you were a child, or is this a newer problem for you?

Um... I guess it's not new. It's been a thing for a while. My mother actually still jokes about my old grade school report cards. She says the teachers always wrote that I was bright, but... I never stayed in my seat. Or I'd blurt out answers. And I'd lose my homework, even when I'd actually done it. So... yeah. Not a new problem.
Beyond the trouble focusing, do you currently feel like you have a hard time sitting still or find yourself acting on impulses without thinking things through?

Um... yeah, I suppose. Sitting still is... hard. Like, if I'm sitting with a client, or... in a chess meeting, my leg is usually bouncing. Or I'll be clicking a pen, or... just turning a cable tie over and over in my fingers. I usually don't realize I'm doing it until somebody finally gives me that look. So... yeah.
When you are in situations where you are expected to remain seated, such as in meetings or during a movie, do you find it difficult to stay in your seat for the entire duration?
Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't think I actually get up and leave. It's mostly just... the fidgeting I mentioned. I usually just stay in my chair.
Do you find that you often interrupt others when they are talking or finish their sentences before they have a chance to finish?

Um... yeah. I guess I do. Mostly at work, with tech stuff. 

The answer just... jumps into my head. So I end up cutting people off, even when I know better. I'll start talking over them, or... sometimes I just grab the keyboard to fix it before they're even finished explaining the problem. So... yeah. I do that.

Looking back at your life, would you say that your tendency to interrupt others or act on impulse has been a frequent, persistent pattern for you, or is it something that happens only once in a while?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't exactly... kept track over the years. I guess I just haven't thought about it that much.

Looking back, would you say that your tendency to act on impulse and your difficulty staying focused have caused problems for you in settings outside of just work, such as in your personal relationships or social life?
Um... I don't know. I guess... maybe? I haven't really noticed it causing major issues outside of work. I mean, my personal life is pretty quiet, so... there's not much to mess up, I suppose.

Thinking back to your childhood, would you say that your tendency to blurt out answers, interrupt others, or struggle to stay in your seat was a daily, persistent struggle, or was it something that only happened occasionally?

Um... I suppose it was pretty constant. My mother... she actually still jokes about it sometimes. She says my old grade school report cards always said I was bright, but... that I never stayed in my seat. And that I'd blurt out answers a lot. Or I'd lose my homework, even when I had actually done it. So... yeah. I guess it was an everyday thing.
If you had to choose which is more disruptive to your daily life right now—the trouble focusing on tasks or the tendency to fidget and act impulsively—which would you say is the bigger problem?
Um... I don't really know. I guess... they both kind of get in the way. I haven't really sat down and compared them, to be honest. It's just... all sort of a mess, I suppose.
When you look at your behavior over the past six months, would you say that your tendency to fidget or act on impulse still happens frequently enough to be a clear, ongoing problem for you?

Um... yeah. I suppose it's still... pretty frequent. Like, if I'm sitting with a client, or... I go to this chess club meeting sometimes... my leg is usually bouncing. Or I'll be clicking a pen, or... twisting a cable tie around in my fingers. Usually until someone gives me a look. So... yeah. Still happens.
In the past six months, how often would you say you find yourself blurting out answers or interrupting others in your daily life?

Um... I guess... pretty often. Especially at work. If someone is explaining a tech issue, I... well, the answer just pops into my head. I end up talking over them. Or... I'll just reach over and grab their keyboard before they're even done talking. I know I shouldn't, but... I just do it anyway.
Aside from the fidgeting and interrupting you mentioned, do you find that you have a hard time waiting for your turn in social situations or lines?

Um... yeah. I suppose so. Like... if I have to wait on hold with a vendor, or... if I'm sitting in a waiting room somewhere... it's just... I get really restless. I feel like I'm going to crawl out of my skin. I end up checking my watch a lot, or... sighing. Or if I'm talking to someone, I just... I try to push the conversation along. Just to get it over with. So... yeah, I guess waiting is hard.
Outside of your work environment, do you find that you struggle with these same difficulties in paying attention to details or staying focused on tasks at home?

Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't... really thought about it, to be honest. At home, I don't really have as many... structured tasks, I guess. So I don't know if I miss details there. I just... haven't really noticed.
In your daily life outside of work, do you find that you frequently make careless mistakes because you have trouble paying close attention to details?

Um... I mean, you asked about outside of work, but... honestly, it's mostly at work where I notice it. Like... I can know a system inside out, but I'll still miss some stupid little thing. 

I'll skip one line in a router setup... or I'll send a client a quote and realize later I put the wrong serial number on it. It's... yeah. Lately, those kinds of slips have been costing me callbacks. People lose trust when you do that. So... I guess that's where I see it most.

When you think about your day-to-day life, would you say that your difficulties with staying focused and your difficulties with impulsivity are equally present, or is one of those two things much more noticeable than the other?
Um... I don't know. I guess I haven't really... weighed them against each other. They just kind of... both happen. I'm not sure which one is worse.
